newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh govt & rebels say drafting peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh govt & rebels say drafting peace deal.

text.p: The government of Bangladesh and tribal rebels on Tuesday continued talks aimed at ending a decades-old insurgency in the country's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts.

"We are working on a draft (peace) agreement," Abdul Hasnat Abdullah, parliamentary chief whip of ruling Awami League and chief government negotiator, told reporters after a second day of negotiation.
Meeting sources said the talks which resumed on Monday would continue on Wednesday.
Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, head of the Parbattya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas, represented the rebel side at the talks.
The current session is the fifth between the government and the PCJSS since Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina began a fresh attempt to end the 23-year-old insurgency.

Officials earlier said broad outlines of a peace treaty had already been agreed at talks between the two sides in May, but the PCJSS was facing opposition from a group of Shanti Bahini hardliners and the Hill Students Council, which backs the insurgency.

Shanti Bahini started the insurgency in 1973 to try to secure autonomy for the 5,500 sq mile (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, and the expulsion of some 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the region.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the protracted bush war, which also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee to Tripura.
Nearly 7,000 refugees returned home in March and April following an agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi, but the date of the next phase of repatriation remains uncertain.
